minutes.headline: ZBA approved a special permit letting a new office building's sign sit closer to the street than the bylaw allows
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals held a public hearing on a special permit request from GCJT Realty LLC (applicant Greg Roy) for a dimensional deviation to place a business sign near a new office building at 1325 Mass Ave closer to the street than the standard 20-ft setback. No members of the public attended to comment; after board questions on lighting hours and sign size, the board voted to approve the permit with the sign set 2 ft from the right-of-way line, subject to standard conditions. The board also elected its chairman and vice chairman for the coming term before adjourning.

what_happened.line: ZBA approved a special permit letting a new office building's sign at 1325 Mass Ave sit closer to the street than the standard setback allows.
The applicant agreed to put the sign's downlighting on a timer rather than lit continuously, addressing a board member's concern about the garage across the street.
The board did not require relief on the secondary sign's size; the applicant will narrow it if the building commissioner finds it exceeds the sign bylaw.
No members of the public attended to comment on the request.
The board elected a chairman and vice chairman for the coming term.

why_it_matters: This sets a dimensional precedent for how close a commercial sign can sit to the street on Mass Ave, a standard other applicants may point to.
Residents near the garage across the street gain a lighting-hours condition tied to this specific approval, not a blanket rule.
The sign's ultimate size still depends on a follow-up check by the building commissioner against the town's sign bylaw.
